subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Adeel can finish a job in 18 days and Zainab can finish it in 9 days. How long will they take working together?
explanation: Together they do 1/18 + 1/9 = 1/6 of the work per day, so they need 6 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A mason can build a wall in 6 days, and his son can build it in 2 days. Working together, in how many days can they build it?
explanation: Together they do 1/6 + 1/2 = 2/3 of the work per day, so they need 1.5 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two printers can complete a print run in 3 hours and 6 hours respectively. How long do they take if both run at once?
explanation: Together they do 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 of the work per hour, so they need 2 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Nida can paint a room in 10 hours; Saad takes 40 hours. How long will they take to paint it together?
explanation: Together they do 1/10 + 1/40 = 1/8 of the work per hour, so they need 8 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A new harvester reaps a field in 36 hours and an older one in 12 hours. If both work together, how long will the field take?
explanation: Together they do 1/36 + 1/12 = 1/9 of the work per hour, so they need 9 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two clerks can clear a pile of files in 20 and 12 days respectively. How many days will they take together?
explanation: Together they do 1/20 + 1/12 = 2/15 of the work per day, so they need 7.5 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A farmer can plough his land in 8 days, and his brother can do it in 24 days. Together they will plough it in:
explanation: Together they do 1/8 + 1/24 = 1/6 of the work per day, so they need 6 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Saad, Mehwish and Imran can do a piece of work in 28, 20 and 5 days respectively. In how many days can they finish it together?
explanation: Combined rate = 1/28 + 1/20 + 1/5 = 2/7, so the time is 3.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Three pumps can empty a flooded basement in 21, 28 and 20 hours respectively. How long will they take working together?
explanation: Combined rate = 1/21 + 1/28 + 1/20 = 2/15, so the time is 7.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Three workers can dig a trench in 30, 20 and 4 days when working alone. How long will they take if all three work together?
explanation: Combined rate = 1/30 + 1/20 + 1/4 = 1/3, so the time is 3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Areeba can do a job in 14 days and Waqas in 21 days. What fraction of the job do they complete in 6 days working together?
explanation: In one day they do 1/14 + 1/21 = 5/42; in 6 they do 5/7.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two men can repair a road in 16 and 20 days respectively. If they work together for 4 days, what part of the road is still left to repair?
explanation: In one day they do 1/16 + 1/20 = 9/80; in 4 they do 9/20, leaving 11/20.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two girls can knit a sweater in 14 hours and 28 hours respectively. What part of the sweater do they finish in one hour working together?
explanation: In one hour they do 1/14 + 1/28 = 3/28; in 1 they do 3/28.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 33 men can build a wall in 4 days. How many days will 22 men take to build the same wall?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If 40 labourers can harvest a field in 18 days, how many labourers are needed to harvest it in 40 days?
explanation: Work = 40 × 18 = 720 man-days; 720/40 = 18 workers.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 22 workers finish a job in 9 days. In how many days would 9 workers finish it?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A contractor needs 28 men to complete a road in 28 days. How many men would he need to finish it in 56 days?
explanation: Work = 28 × 28 = 784 man-days; 784/56 = 14 workers.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 25 tailors take 6 days to stitch a school’s uniforms. How long will 15 tailors take?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: It takes 18 painters 33 hours to paint a hall. How many painters are needed to paint it in 22 hours?
explanation: Work = 18 × 33 = 594 man-hours; 594/22 = 27 workers.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 21 men working 7 hours a day complete a job in 4 days. How many days will 12 men working 7 hours a day take to complete it?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A factory with 7 workers working 8 hours daily finishes an order in 16 days. How many hours a day must 16 workers work to finish the same order in 7 days?
explanation: Work = 7 × 8 × 16 = 896 man-hours; hours per day = 896/(16 × 7) = 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 5 carpenters can make 35 chairs in 7 days. How many days will 9 carpenters take to make 45 chairs?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If 5 workers can lay 40 metres of pipe in 8 days, how many metres can 7 workers lay in 7 days?
explanation: One worker lays 40/(5 × 8) m a day; 7 workers in 7 days lay 49 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 8 men undertake to finish a job in 33 days. After 9 days, 4 more men join them. In how many more days will the job be completed?
explanation: Work left = 8 × 24 = 192 man-days; with 12 men it takes 16 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A team of 15 workers was to complete a building in 28 days. After 18 days, 5 workers left. How many more days will the rest take to finish the building?
explanation: Work left = 15 × 10 = 150 man-days; with 10 men it takes 15 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 7 men and 10 women complete a piece of work in 8 days. If one man does the work of 2 women, how many days will 6 men and 4 women take to do it?
explanation: In woman-units: 7 × 2 + 10 = 24 units for 8 days = 192; new team = 16 units, so 192/16 = 12 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man works 3 times as fast as a boy. 15 men and 11 boys can finish a task in 30 days. In how many days can 12 men and 6 boys finish it?
explanation: In woman-units: 15 × 3 + 11 = 56 units for 30 days = 1680; new team = 42 units, so 1680/42 = 40 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 15 men and 6 women can reap a field in 11 days. If a man does as much work as 2 women, how long will 9 men alone take?
explanation: In woman-units: 15 × 2 + 6 = 36 units for 11 days = 396; new team = 18 units, so 396/18 = 22 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 3 men or 10 women can finish a job in 27 days. How many days will 3 men and 8 women take working together?
explanation: 3 men = 10 women, so 1 man = 10/3 women; the job is 270 woman-days; 3 men and 8 women = 18 women, taking 15 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A task can be done by 5 men in 21 days or by 19 women in 21 days. In how many days can 5 men and 2 women do it?
explanation: 5 men = 19 women, so 1 man = 19/5 women; the job is 399 woman-days; 5 men and 2 women = 21 women, taking 19 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A field can be ploughed by 12 large tractors or by 4 small tractors in 22 days. How long will 3 large and 3 small tractors take together?
explanation: 12 men = 4 women, so 1 man = 1/3 women; the job is 88 woman-days; 3 men and 3 women = 4 women, taking 22 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 13 men and 4 women can complete a project in 25 days. If a man works 3 times as fast as a woman, how many women working alone would be needed to finish it in 5 days?
explanation: Work = (13 × 3 + 4) × 25 = 1075 woman-days; in 5 days this needs 215 women.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 2 men and 6 women finish a job in 21 days. Taking one man’s work as equal to that of 2 women, how many men alone could finish it in 5 days?
explanation: Work = (2 × 2 + 6) × 21 = 210 woman-days; in 5 days this needs 42 women = 21 men.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Omer and Hamza can do a job in 30 and 15 days respectively. They work together for 6 days, after which Omer leaves. How many more days will Hamza take to finish the job?
explanation: In 6 together they finish 3/5; the remaining 2/5 takes the second worker 2/5 × 15 = 6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two workers can finish a project alone in 9 days and 6 days. They start together, but the first worker quits after 3 days. How long does the second worker need to complete the rest?
explanation: In 3 together they finish 5/6; the remaining 1/6 takes the second worker 1/6 × 6 = 1.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 22 and 11 minutes respectively. Both are opened together, and P is closed after 4 minutes. How much longer will Q take to fill the tank?
explanation: In 4 together they finish 6/11; the remaining 5/11 takes the second worker 5/11 × 11 = 5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Rabia can build a boundary wall in 6 days and Naveed can build it in 30 days. Rabia works alone for 3 days and then Naveed finishes the wall. How many days does Naveed work?
explanation: In 3 days the first does 1/2; the remaining 1/2 takes the second 1/2 × 30 = 15 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tailor can finish an order in 6 days and his assistant in 18 days. The tailor works on it for 5 days and then hands it over to the assistant. How long does the assistant take to finish?
explanation: In 5 days the first does 5/6; the remaining 1/6 takes the second 1/6 × 18 = 3 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Amna and Faisal can do a piece of work in 4 and 20 days respectively. They start together, but Amna leaves 2 days before the work is finished. In how many days is the work completed?
explanation: The second works all T days, the first T − 2: T/20 + (T − 2)/4 = 1 ⇒ T = 5 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two masons can build a room in 28 and 14 days. They begin together, but the first mason leaves 5 days before the room is finished. How many days does the building take in all?
explanation: The second works all T days, the first T − 5: T/14 + (T − 5)/28 = 1 ⇒ T = 11 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A job can be done by P in 6 days and by Q in 27 days. They start together, and P stops working 5 days before the job ends. What is the total time taken?
explanation: The second works all T days, the first T − 5: T/27 + (T − 5)/6 = 1 ⇒ T = 9 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and a leak empties the full tank in 14 hours. With the leak, how long does the pipe take to fill the tank?
explanation: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/14 = 2/21, so the tank fills in 10.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An inlet can fill a cistern in 12 minutes while an outlet can empty it in 30 minutes. If both are open, how long will the empty cistern take to fill?
explanation: Net rate = 1/12 − 1/30 = 1/20, so the tank fills in 20.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tap can fill a bath in 15 minutes, but the drain empties it in 24 minutes. If the plug is left out, how long does the bath take to fill?
explanation: Net rate = 1/15 − 1/24 = 1/40, so the tank fills in 40.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A swimming pool is filled by a pump in 12 hours and emptied by a drain in 16 hours. How long does filling take if the drain is accidentally left open?
explanation: Net rate = 1/12 − 1/16 = 1/48, so the tank fills in 48.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tank is normally filled in 20 hours, but because of a leak it takes 30 hours. How long would the leak take to empty the full tank?
explanation: Leak rate = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so the leak alone empties it in 60.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A pipe fills a drum in 7 minutes. Owing to a hole in the bottom, it now takes 9 minutes. In what time would the hole empty the full drum?
explanation: Leak rate = 1/7 − 1/9 = 2/63, so the leak alone empties it in 31.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 2 and 3 hours, and a third pipe can empty it in 6 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
explanation: Net rate = 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/6 = 2/3, so the time is 1.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Taps X and Y fill a tank in 11 and 15 minutes, while tap Z empties it in 15 minutes. How long does the empty tank take to fill if all three are opened?
explanation: Net rate = 1/11 + 1/15 − 1/15 = 1/11, so the time is 11.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in 3 hours?
explanation: Each hour it fills 1/8 of the tank; after 3 hours 3/8 is full.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tap fills a 3,440-litre tank at 80 litres a minute. How long will it take to fill the tank?
explanation: Time = 3440/80 = 43 minutes.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A drain empties a full tank in 18 hours. What part of the water remains in the tank after 5 hours?
explanation: Each hour it empties 1/18 of the tank; after 5 hours 5/18 has gone and 13/18 remains.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two pipes fill a tank in 12 and 6 hours respectively. How long will they take together to fill half the tank?
explanation: Together they fill the tank in 4 hours, so half the tank takes 2 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Faisal and Maria together can finish a job in 15 days. Faisal alone can finish it in 40 days. How long would Maria take alone?
explanation: Other’s rate = 1/15 − 1/40 = 1/24, so alone it takes 24.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two taps together fill a tank in 5 hours. One of them alone fills it in 30 hours. How long does the other tap take on its own?
explanation: Other’s rate = 1/5 − 1/30 = 1/6, so alone it takes 6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A father and son together can mow a lawn in 10 hours. The father alone takes 30 hours. How long would the son take by himself?
explanation: Other’s rate = 1/10 − 1/30 = 1/15, so alone it takes 15.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two machines working together finish an order in 5 days. The newer machine alone would take 6 days. How long would the older machine take on its own?
explanation: Other’s rate = 1/5 − 1/6 = 1/30, so alone it takes 30.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Working together, two typists can type a thesis in 9 hours. If one of them can type it alone in 36 hours, the other alone would take:
explanation: Other’s rate = 1/9 − 1/36 = 1/12, so alone it takes 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Zainab and Usman can do a job in 18 days, Usman and Salman in 9 days, and Zainab and Salman in 12 days. How long will all three take working together?
explanation: Adding the pair rates counts everyone twice: 1/18 + 1/9 + 1/12 = 1/4 = 2 × (all three); so all three take 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 24 hours, B and C in 10 hours, and A and C in 8 hours. How long do all three take together?
explanation: Adding the pair rates counts everyone twice: 1/24 + 1/10 + 1/8 = 4/15 = 2 × (all three); so all three take 7.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Hamza works four times as fast as Ali. Together they finish a job in 12 days. How long would Ali take alone?
explanation: Rates are in the ratio 4:1; together 5 parts finish in 12, so the slower (1 part) alone takes 60 and the faster takes 15.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A new machine works twice as fast as an old one. Together they complete an order in 8 hours. How long would the new machine take alone?
explanation: Rates are in the ratio 2:1; together 3 parts finish in 8, so the slower (1 part) alone takes 24 and the faster takes 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Sana is three times as efficient as Ayesha, and Sana alone can finish a task in 14 days. How long will they take working together?
explanation: The slower one takes 3 × 14 = 42 days; together 1/14 + 1/42 = 2/21, i.e. 10.5 days.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Ali can finish a job in 29 days. What fraction of the job does he do in 7 days?
explanation: Each day does 1/29; after 7, 7/29 is done.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Farah can type a report in 17 hours. What fraction of it does she type in 12 hours?
explanation: Each day does 1/17; after 12, 12/17 is done.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A builder completes a house in 29 weeks. What part of the house is still unfinished after 4 weeks?
explanation: Each week does 1/29; after 4, 4/29 is done and 25/29 is left.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If a man can do 2/3 of a job in 16 days, how long will he take to do the whole job?
explanation: 2/3 of the job takes 16, so 1/3 takes 8 and the whole takes 24.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A pipe fills 2/5 of a tank in 16 minutes. How long will it take to fill the whole tank?
explanation: 2/5 of the job takes 16, so 1/5 takes 8 and the whole takes 40.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Sadia reads 1/9 of a novel in 6 days. At the same rate, how many days does she need for the whole novel?
explanation: 1/9 of the job takes 6, so 1/9 takes 6 and the whole takes 54.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A worker has done 3/5 of a job in 9 days. How many more days will he need to finish it?
explanation: 3/5 of the job takes 9, so 1/5 takes 3 and the whole takes 15; 15 − 9 = 6 more.

q: Kamran ate 3/7 of a pizza and Saad ate 1/3 of it. What fraction of the pizza did they eat between them?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tank is 5/12 full. After water equal to 1/4 of its capacity is drawn off, what fraction of the tank is full?
explanation: Using the LCM 12: 5/12 − 1/4 = 1/6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: By how much does 1/2 exceed 1/7?
explanation: Using the LCM 14: 1/2 − 1/7 = 5/14.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the value of 1/3 of 2/3.
explanation: Multiply numerators and denominators: 1/3 × 2/3 = 2/9.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Evaluate: 1/7 × 1/6
explanation: Multiply numerators and denominators: 1/7 × 1/6 = 1/42.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Divide 1/5 by 1/9.
explanation: Dividing by 1/9 means multiplying by 9: 1 4/5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tailor used 4 3/7 metres of cloth for a shirt and 2 1/2 metres for a pair of trousers. How much cloth did he use in all?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the reciprocal of 1 2/3?
explanation: 1 2/3 = 5/3, so its reciprocal is 3/5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Multiply 0.02 by 0.7.
explanation: 2 × 7 = 14; there are 3 decimal places in all, so the product is 0.014.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The product of 0.3 and 0.06 is:
explanation: 3 × 6 = 18; there are 3 decimal places in all, so the product is 0.018.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Work out the quotient 0.1 ÷ 0.5.
explanation: Multiply both by a power of ten to clear the divisor’s decimals: 0.1 ÷ 0.5 = 0.2.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 9.6 is divided by 0.8. What is the quotient?
explanation: Multiply both by a power of ten to clear the divisor’s decimals: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 = 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Take 0.085 away from 1.5. What remains?
explanation: Line up the decimal points: 1.5 − 0.085 = 1.415.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bag of flour weighs 0.77 kg and a bag of sugar weighs 0.27 kg. What is their total weight?
explanation: Line up the decimal points: 0.77 + 0.27 = 1.04 kg.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Express 9/25 as a decimal.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Write 0.28 as a fraction in its lowest terms.
explanation: 0.28 = 280/1000 = 7/25 in lowest terms.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How many pieces of ribbon, each 0.6 m long, can be cut from a ribbon 9.6 m long?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If one litre of cooking oil weighs 0.83 kg, how much do 18 litres weigh?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Calculate the decimal value of (0.5 × 0.3) ÷ 0.05.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The recurring decimal 0.444… is equal to:
explanation: One recurring digit: 0.44… = 4/9.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Which fraction is equal to 0.555…?
explanation: One recurring digit: 0.55… = 5/9.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Express the recurring decimal 0.878787… as a fraction in its lowest terms.
explanation: Two recurring digits: 87/99 = 29/33.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Convert 0.484848… into a common fraction.
explanation: Two recurring digits: 48/99 = 16/33.
